definition: A written outline of what a lesson will cover and in what order.
business_context_example: The lesson plan said forty minutes. The first activity took forty minutes.

definition: The list of what a course will teach, in the order it teaches it.
business_context_example: The syllabus promises the past perfect in week six. Week six is always optimistic.

definition: A sheet given to students during a lesson.
business_context_example: Twelve students, eleven handouts, and one very specific silence.

definition: An activity students do in twos rather than alone.
business_context_example: Pair work is how the quiet half of the room finally says something.

definition: Repeating a form until saying it stops requiring thought.
business_context_example: Nobody enjoys a drill on Monday and everybody uses it on Thursday.

definition: A short activity at the start of a lesson to get people talking.
business_context_example: A good warmer takes five minutes. A great one takes five and nobody notices.

definition: A short review of what has already been covered.
business_context_example: Start with a recap. Half of them were mentally on the bus last week.

definition: A class where students are at noticeably different levels.
business_context_example: Every mixed-ability class has one person who finishes early and reads the ceiling.

definition: Whether students actually come to the lessons they signed up for.
business_context_example: Attendance is excellent until the first sunny Friday in May.

definition: The percentage of students who stop before the course ends.
business_context_example: Our drop-out rate is 18%, and most of it lands the week the gyms go quiet.

definition: A written summary of how a student is doing.
business_context_example: Write the progress report as though the student will read it, because they will.

definition: A private lesson with a single student.
business_context_example: In a one-to-one there is nowhere to hide, which is the entire point.

definition: A test that decides which level a new student joins.
business_context_example: Everybody thinks the placement test put them one level too low.

definition: What a student should be able to do by the end of a lesson.
business_context_example: If the learning objective doesn't start with a verb, it isn't one.

definition: To reach the level of the others after falling behind.
business_context_example: She missed three weeks and caught up in one, which nobody mentions to the others.

definition: Everything a school teaches across all its courses.
business_context_example: The curriculum is reviewed every summer and changed every third one.

definition: One self-contained part of a longer course.
business_context_example: Six modules, and everyone remembers the one with the role play.

definition: A group of students who start at the same time.
business_context_example: The September intake is twice the size of the February one, every single year.

definition: The hours a student actually spends with a teacher.
business_context_example: Sixty contact hours sounds like a lot until you divide it by a year.

definition: A course that mixes lessons in a room with work done online.
business_context_example: Blended learning works when somebody checks the online half. Somebody rarely does.

definition: Work a student does alone, between lessons.
business_context_example: Self-study is where the course is actually won, and where it quietly stops.

definition: Something a student must already have before joining a course.
business_context_example: The prerequisite is B1. The prerequisite is treated as a suggestion.

definition: The process of signing students up for a course.
business_context_example: Enrolment peaks every January, when the whole country briefly believes in itself.

definition: The department that decides who is accepted onto a course.
business_context_example: Admissions closes at five. The best application arrives at four fifty-eight.

definition: A day when the public can visit and see the school.
business_context_example: An open day sells more courses than any advert, and costs a tray of biscuits.

definition: The money a student pays for the teaching itself.
business_context_example: Nobody argues about the tuition fee. They argue about the deposit.

definition: Paying the fee in agreed parts instead of all at once.
business_context_example: An instalment plan doubled our January enrolments and cost us nothing.

definition: The official start and end dates of each teaching period.
business_context_example: Publish the term dates in June. Parents plan holidays before you plan lessons.

definition: A free or cheap first lesson so somebody can try the course before paying.
business_context_example: Nine of ten adults who take a trial lesson sign up. The tenth was sent by their employer.

definition: The person in charge of a school.
business_context_example: The head teacher teaches four hours a week and apologises for it constantly.

definition: The plan of which class happens when and where.
business_context_example: The timetable is finished on Friday and wrong by Monday.

definition: To teach somebody else's class while they are away.
business_context_example: Whoever is in the staff room at 8:55 is covering the nine o'clock.

definition: How many students are in one group.
business_context_example: Class size eight is the number everyone promises and twelve is the number that pays.

definition: Official recognition that a school meets a required standard.
business_context_example: Accreditation takes nine months and is mentioned in every advert for nine years.

definition: An official visit to check how a school is run.
business_context_example: The week before an inspection is the tidiest the building will ever be.

definition: The money a school earns from the fees students pay.
business_context_example: Fee income looks healthy in October and lonely in July.

definition: How much of your rooms and teaching hours are actually used.
business_context_example: Three empty rooms at ten in the morning is a utilisation problem, not a sales one.

definition: Any way of measuring what a student can do.
business_context_example: Assessment tells the student where they are. The grade tells everybody else.

definition: A practice exam run under real exam conditions.
business_context_example: The mock exam exists so the real one is the second time, not the first.

definition: Reading student work and giving it a grade.
business_context_example: Marking expands to fill every evening you were planning to have.

definition: The lowest score that counts as a pass.
business_context_example: The pass mark is 60. Somebody always gets 59 and remembers it for years.

definition: To take an exam again after failing it.
business_context_example: The resit group is smaller, quieter and far better prepared.

definition: The mark given for a piece of work or a whole course.
business_context_example: Give the grade and the reason in the same sentence, or you'll give both twice.

definition: The document proving somebody completed a course.
business_context_example: Adults say the certificate doesn't matter, then photograph it in the car park.

definition: The room where teachers work between lessons.
business_context_example: Everything important about a school is decided in the staff room at 10:40.

definition: A meeting of all the teachers.
business_context_example: A staff meeting is forty minutes long and contains eleven minutes of meeting.

definition: An evening when teachers meet students' parents.
business_context_example: Parents' evening runs from six to eight and finishes at nine twenty.

definition: A teacher brought in temporarily to replace another.
business_context_example: The class tests a supply teacher for exactly four minutes, then settles.

definition: The phrase that reorganises a teacher's entire morning.
business_context_example: "The photocopier is down" has ended more lesson plans than any inspection.

definition: The last days before a teaching period stops.
business_context_example: By the end of term the students are tired and the teachers are a different tired.
